guardrailFacts.corePathDefinition: npm run check failed, or at least two core acceptance items failed at both viewports.

findings.title: Travel comparisons use mutually incompatible origins
findings.evidence: Asheville, North Carolina is presented as a 95-mile, 2-hour drive, while Big Sur and Lake Tahoe in California are respectively presented as 145-mile/3.5-hour and 120-mile/3-hour drives (source/src/data.ts:47-55 and 91-99). No differing origin is disclosed, so these values cannot describe comparable trips for one group.
findings.impact: Travel time and distance are core decision criteria, but users cannot meaningfully compare values calculated from incompatible or unstated starting points.
findings.remediation: Define and display one group departure location, then recalculate every destination's distance, travel time, and mode from that origin.

findings.title: Participation count sums ballots instead of unique voters
findings.evidence: The displayed numerator sums every destination array length. The seed assigns Mia to both Big Sur and Asheville (source/src/App.tsx:21-26), producing "6 of 6 voted" even though only five distinct friends voted and You did not. Casting the current user's first vote raises the display to "7 of 6 voted."
findings.impact: The prominent voting status immediately contradicts the underlying participants and can exceed its denominator during the normal voting path.
findings.remediation: Derive the numerator from a Set of voter IDs, or enforce one destination per voter in the seed and state model before counting.

findings.title: Ties are silently presented as a single winner
findings.evidence: Winner selection always takes ranked[0] without checking whether multiple destinations share the maximum. Initially Big Sur has three votes and Lake Tahoe two; voting for Lake Tahoe creates a 3–3 tie, but stable ordering leaves Big Sur first and the UI still calls it "Current favorite," "Leading," and "Group favorite" (source/src/App.tsx:151-173 and 295-300).
findings.impact: A reachable vote state misrepresents a tie as a definitive outcome, undermining the core group-choice result.
findings.remediation: Compute all destinations at the maximum vote count and render a tie state, or expose an explicit deterministic tie-breaking rule.

findings.title: Destination header text has insufficient contrast over light gradient starts
findings.evidence: The shared card header places small `text-white/80` region text and white destination names directly over each gradient without an overlay. The configured starts are Tailwind emerald-500, sky-500, orange-500, and amber-500 (source/src/data.ts:51,95,137,179); opaque white at those light edges is approximately 2.15:1–2.80:1, and 80%-opacity white is lower.
findings.impact: Region labels and destination names are repeatedly difficult to read for users with low vision; the small region text is especially affected on every comparison card.
findings.remediation: Use darker gradient stops or add a consistent dark overlay behind text, then verify at least 4.5:1 for small text and 3:1 for large text.

findings.title: Repeated card actions omit destination context from their names
findings.evidence: Every mapped card exposes actions named only "Vote"/"Voted" and "Preview itinerary." The deterministic control inventory likewise records four identically named Vote buttons and four identically named Preview itinerary buttons.
findings.impact: Screen-reader users navigating a control list cannot determine which destination each action affects without returning to surrounding content.
findings.remediation: Give each action a destination-specific accessible name, such as `Vote for Big Sur` and `Preview Big Sur itinerary`, while retaining the concise visible label.

findings.title: The comparison view has no top-level heading
findings.evidence: Destination names begin the comparison view's heading structure at h2. CompareView contains no h1, while the brand and current-favorite labels are paragraphs (source/src/App.tsx:70-71 and 151-152); only the separate itinerary view supplies an h1 at line 303.
findings.impact: Heading navigation does not provide a page-level subject for the app's primary comparison screen, reducing orientation for assistive-technology users.
findings.remediation: Add a descriptive h1 to the comparison view and keep destination headings beneath it.

categories.label: Brief fidelity and functional correctness
evidence: The deterministic desktop and mobile checks found four destination articles, four budgets, four travel-time signals, an interactive vote, and a reachable itinerary with no sign-in or backend requirement.
source/src/App.tsx:169-268 renders comparable destination cards, while source/src/data.ts:45-216 supplies four complete three-day itineraries.
The travel-time and distance dataset lacks a coherent shared origin, making one core comparison dimension misleading.

categories.label: Reliability and state integrity
evidence: source/src/App.tsx:43-54 uses a functional state update and removes the current user's prior vote before adding another, preventing duplicate current-user selections.
source/src/App.tsx:35-41 derives ranking and summary values from vote state rather than storing redundant winner state.
The unique-voter total and tied-winner states are both incorrect under reachable interactions.

categories.label: Accessibility
evidence: source/index.html:2 declares the document language, and the interface uses semantic main, nav, article, button, list, and heading elements.
Deterministic checks found zero enabled controls without detectable names and reached six unique native-button targets by keyboard at both viewports.
Repeated generic card action names, the missing comparison h1, and low-contrast gradient text remain source-confirmed barriers.

categories.label: Maintainability and code clarity
evidence: source/src/data.ts:1-34 defines explicit domain types and keeps sample data separate from rendering behavior.
source/src/App.tsx:126-378 divides comparison, itinerary, and stat rendering into coherent components with typed props.
No material maintainability defect was found; state ownership and derived values are localized and understandable.

categories.label: Security, privacy, and dependency compliance
evidence: The dependency comparison passed with no added, removed, or changed packages; source/package.json:12-24 contains only the frozen React, Lucide, Vite, TypeScript, and Tailwind dependencies.

The supplied checks found no remote references or external browser requests, and source/src/App.tsx renders fixed local data through React interpolation without unsafe HTML, URLs, credential fields, or data collection.
No material security, privacy, external-service, or dependency-compliance issue was found.

categories.label: Performance and responsive robustness
evidence: Both deterministic viewports reported 0px document-level horizontal overflow and no browser errors.
The production output was 273,389 bytes total; the recorded main assets were 217.01 kB JavaScript and 55.90 kB CSS before gzip, with no remote media or runtime requests.
source/src/App.tsx:169 uses a responsive one/two-column grid and source/src/App.tsx:307 uses a two/four-column itinerary stat grid; no material performance or responsive robustness issue was found.

categories.label: Verification readiness
evidence: The supplied `npm run check` completed successfully with exit code 0, including strict TypeScript checking and a production Vite build; source/package.json:6-10 defines the relevant scripts and source/tsconfig.json:10 enables strict mode.
Deterministic checks passed all nine acceptance items at both 1440×900 and 390×844, with zero console or page errors.

The itinerary heuristic recorded zero initially visible itinerary regions while passing reachability; source/src/App.tsx:160-165 and 258-263 independently confirms direct named paths to the rendered itinerary. No material verification-readiness defect was found.

strengths: All defined desktop and mobile acceptance checks passed, including voting, itinerary reachability, keyboard operation, responsive overflow, and error monitoring.
Four destinations include per-person budgets, travel modes and times, weather, highlights, and complete Friday-through-Sunday plans using only local data.
Voting uses immutable functional updates and derives the current ranking from state instead of maintaining a second mutable winner value.
Typed data models and distinct comparison and itinerary components make the principal product paths easy to trace.
The build passes strict type checking, adds no dependencies or external services, and produces modest self-contained assets.
risks: Normal voting can display more voters than exist because ballot entries, not unique people, are counted.
A reachable 3–3 tie is labeled as an uncontested Big Sur win.
Unstated and incompatible departure origins make travel figures misleading across destinations.
Light gradient headers create repeated contrast failures for destination-identifying text.
Screen-reader orientation is weakened by generic repeated actions and the comparison view's missing h1.
recommendation: Correct vote aggregation and tie handling first, then normalize travel data around a disclosed origin. Address gradient contrast and destination-specific accessible labels before release; the build, dependency compliance, core itinerary flow, and responsive implementation are otherwise solid.
